policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, choose the color this way: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again (a color once started is finished before any other color is touched); only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start with the color of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) whose color is still needed and which is not set aside by the bin-proximity clause below; at step #1 that is the needed-color cube nearest the bin's center, of whichever needed color it is. Do not choose the start color by required count or by a fixed color preference. Among the cubes of that color, first set aside every cube whose remembered or detected position lies within about 40 px of the bin center, as long as some other cube of that color lies farther from the bin (a near-bin cube is picked only when it is the last cube of its color on the table). Among the cubes that remain, pick the oldest one on the table: point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color and is not set aside. If the scene at this decision step shows a detection of that color within about 10 px of that entry, point at that detection's center; if not (the arm may be covering it), point at the remembered position. After the bin-proximity set-aside, the age order in `cubes` is the only criterion among same-colored cubes: do not choose the cube nearest the gripper, nearest the button, nearest the bin (except as the step #1 tie-break among start cubes, below), or the one with the smallest y. The target is the detection of that color within about 10 px of the chosen entry in the scene at this decision step; a detection that has drifted a few pixels is still the same cube, so do not discard it, and never point at a detection lying within about 10 px of the bin center. At step #1 the first entry of `cubes` is the needed-color cube nearest the bin's center. A point offset by a pixel or two from the detection center is acceptable; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first entry of `cubes` whose color is still needed, and if `cubes` has no such entry, choose A pointing at any visible cube of a needed color, or failing that any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), write placed=[] explicitly: the field is always output as an explicit list, even when empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Write the list as a JSON array with double-quoted strings, never Python-style single quotes; the field is compared literally. e.g. ["green", "green"]

fields.name: cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each as [color, [y, x]]. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), list every visible cube of a goal color ordered by distance to the bin's center, nearest first (ties: smaller y). Otherwise copy the carried-in list and: remove an entry only if the execution steps shown at THIS step include the fingers closing (about 100% to about 46% open) within about 10 px of that entry and the cube then reported 'held in the gripper'; if the shown steps begin with a cube already held, remove nothing for it. Then for every goal-color detection in the shown steps (excluding the one marked 'held in the gripper', any detection within about 10 px of the held cube's position while it is held, and any detection within about 10 px of the reported bin center), find the carried entry within about 10 px of it: if one exists, that entry keeps its slot and takes the newest position; if none exists, append a new entry at the end, in order of first appearance. A cube reported 20 px or more from the bin center is a real table cube and is entered even if it showed up just after a release; a cube that vanishes for a frame or two because the arm covers it keeps its entry and is not re-added. Never reorder entries, never drop-and-re-append: the list order is the age order and nothing seen later changes it. Example of a refresh: carried [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [71, 154]]] with a green reported at [68, 160] becomes [["blue", [117, 71]], ["green", [68, 160]]]. Cubes of colors not named in the goal are never entered. Write it as a JSON array with double-quoted color strings. e.g. [["blue", [54, 118]], ["blue", [87, 181]]]
